We need to propose a retrosynthesis route with 3 reactions for target SMILES: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2)cc1

We have guidance: steps are (forward) 1) carboxylic acid to amide (coupling). 2) Doebner modification to form α,β-unsaturated acid (alkene). 3) sulfonamide formation from sulfonyl chloride and amine.

Thus retrosynthetic direction: break amide bond to give carboxylic acid and aniline (aniline is Nc3ccccc3N? Actually amide is C(=O)N attached to aniline (c3ccccc3N). So disconnection: target -> amide precursor: carboxylic acid (with α,β-unsaturated chain attached to aromatic sulfone) and aniline (para-aminophenyl?). Wait structure: .../C=C/C(=O)N c3ccccc3N . So amide carbonyl attached to aniline (aniline is aniline with an extra NH2 at para? Actually c3ccccc3N is an aniline (aniline). So amide formed between carboxylic acid (α,β-unsaturated) and aniline.

Next, the α,β-unsaturated acid derived from Doebner modification of aromatic aldehyde with malonic acid. The aldehyde part is the aromatic ring attached to sulfonyl group: c2ccc(... )cc2 where the substituent is the α,β-unsaturated chain attached via double bond to the aromatic ring. So the aldehyde precursor would be aromatic aldehyde (c2ccc(CHO)cc2) attached to sulfonyl group.

Thus retrosynthesis steps:

Step 1 (reverse of amide coupling): break amide to give carboxylic acid (α,β-unsaturated acid) and aniline (c3ccccc3N). So we need template for amide formation (carboxylic acid + amine -> amide). Use template ID from search? We didn't find. Could use generic template ID maybe known. Could search for amide formation with functional_groups_formed amide. Let's search again with functional_groups_formed ["amide"] and maybe also functional_groups_broken ["carboxylic acid"] but need correct group name "carboxylic acid" is not valid; must be "aliphatic carboxylic acid" or "aromatic carboxylic acid". Our acid is aromatic? The acid is attached to aromatic ring (aryl). So functional group is aromatic carboxylic acid. Use that.
